bullets.text: ROE reached 36.0% vs 34.7% in 1992; underwriting margin was 10.7%; net income rose 74% to $267.3M ($3.58/share); operating income increased 52% to $197.3M ($2.61/share), achieving best ever financial results.

Multi-year re-engineering shifts focus from niche nonstandard coverage to low-cost broad auto insurance; redefines business as reducing accident trauma and costs, intentionally targeting lower 4% underwriting margins to deter competition and regulation.
NPW grew 25% to record $1,819.2M vs $1,451.2M in 1992; Core business NPW increased 25% to $1,700M (93% of total); Diversified divisions generated $118M NPW and $43.7M in service revenues.

Core underwriting expense ratio dropped to 25.9% from 28.4% toward a 20% goal by 2000; direct premiums per employee rose to $322,000 from $228,000 as five-year direct premiums grew 47% on 4% headcount growth.
Loss and handling expenses were 63.7% of earned premium; LAE ratio decreased to 9.1% from 10.7%; 56% of third-party property damage and collision claims closed within seven days vs 51% in 1992.

Invested assets reached $2,786.4M; after-tax investment income was $177.2M; realized capital gains totaled $107.9M ($74.3M from MBNA sale); raised $177M selling stock to support expansion and $350M in debt.

Average rates were reduced 0.8% across existing private passenger auto programs via lower expenses and controlled losses, versus a 1.9% increase in 1992; growth will be curtailed if underwriting profit drops below 4%.

Wrote $64M in standard and preferred auto (4.5% of private auto premiums); targets $115B potential vehicle market where Progressive holds 1.5% share; now or soon will offer three price levels with differing commissions.

Community Marketing tests continued in Miami and Tampa with multi-channel purchasing via phone, mail, office, and agents; 1-800-AUTO-PRO in Florida provides comparison rates against State Farm, Allstate, and Prudential.

New gainsharing bonus paid $23.4M to employees for 1993 performance; transitioned corporate structure to dynamic cross-functional teams and Process Leadership under Total Quality Management to replace rigid hierarchies.
